senses.gloss:
tuṣṭi
(‘complacency’)
------------------------------------------
The Sāṅkhyakārikā (verse 50) of ईश्वरकृष्ण (circa A. D. 400) lists nine kinds of तुष्टि or complacency.
Of these, four are आध्यात्मिक (concerning the Self) and five are bāhya (external, concerning wealth and desire).
The आध्यात्मिक tuṣṭis are:
The complacency that comes as a result of the teaching of the गुरु (preceptor) that one is the पुरुष (the Self) different from प्रकृति (insentient nature) and yet making no attempt to get release, is prakṛtituṣṭi.
The complacency that comes as a result of adopting monastic life, thinking that, that itself is enough to attain लिबेरतिओन्, is upādānatuṣṭi.
The complacency that comes out of the conviction that लिबेरतिओन् comes automatically in course of time, is kālatuṣṭi.
The complacency that comes as a result of the belief that luck is the real cause of लिबेरतिओन्, is bhāgya-तुष्टि.
The bāhyatuṣṭis are:
Realising the difficulties involved in the acquisition of wealth and getting detached towards it, is because of pāratuṣṭi.
Realising the troubles involved in protecting one’s wealth and getting detached from it, is supāratuṣṭi.
Realising that the wealth acquired by so much trouble gets exhausted very soon by spending it, leading to great worry, and hence getting detached from it is parāparatuṣṭi.
Realising that the desire to enjoy the objects of pleasure increases by enjoyment, leading to misery, and getting detached from them is anuttamāmbhas-तुष्टि.
Realising that one is causing injury to others while trying to acquire the objects of pleasure, and hence getting detached towards them is uttamāmbhas-तुष्टि.
Absence of these tuṣṭis is an obstacle in the path of कैवल्य or लिबेरतिओन्.
